info.title: Periapsis Incident Management API
info.description:
Canonical HTTP contract for Periapsis. Authentication authority is held in
server-side sessions; tenant and platform authorization is always re-evaluated
by backend use cases and never inferred from client-visible state.

tags.name: DFIR
tags.description:
Case- and Alert-scoped indicators, assets, evidence, timeline, tasks,
attachments, and relationships. DFIR commands accepting Idempotency-Key use
immutable receipts with a 24-hour default lifetime from the original command.
Database lifetime bounds are 24 hours through 7 days; the current default does
not guarantee seven days of replay, and retries do not extend receipt expiry.
Within that window, an exact authorized replay returns the original historical
mutation result, not a later live revision. Every replay rechecks current
authorization, including all current linked roots for shared IOC/asset writes;
historical receipts never preserve revoked authority or a stale related-root
projection. Keys bind the tenant, actor user, operation, membership epoch,
root, resource identifiers, result revision, and canonical request.
Consumed key digests and caller-owned create identifiers remain permanently
reserved in their tenant/user/operation and tenant/resource-kind scopes,
respectively. An authorized retry with an expired key returns 409, both before
and after receipt cleanup; pruning never permits that key or an old create
identifier to be reused. Upload-prepare replay additionally requires the
original live pending pair and unexpired upload grant described by those
operations; the receipt lifetime is not an upload-capability lifetime.

get.summary: Check whether the API process is alive

200.description: The process is running.

get.summary: Check whether the API can receive traffic

200.description: Required dependencies are ready.

get.summary: Get one authorized Alert projection
get.description: The backend selects an operator or customer-safe projection from live authority; an identifier or a prior UI action never grants access.

200.description: Current Alert projection.

delete.summary: Reversibly tombstone one Alert
delete.description:
The backend re-resolves the exact live Alert, human operator, scoped
alert.delete authority, and current version. The Alert disappears from
every ordinary projection while append-only audit and retention evidence
remain. If-Match and expectedVersion must identify the same live version;
an exact idempotent replay returns the original tombstone receipt.

200.description: Alert tombstoned once or the exact prior receipt replayed.

put.summary: Replace the editable core metadata of one Alert
put.description:
The backend reloads the exact tenant-owned Alert and re-evaluates the
operator's live alert.update scope. If-Match binds the current Alert
version. The idempotency key is bound to the complete normalized
replacement and expected version; an exact authorized replay returns the
immutable original command result even if a later unrelated mutation has
advanced the Alert. Reuse with a different replacement returns 409.

200.description: Exact metadata replacement committed once, or its immutable result replayed.

get.summary: List the operators watching one Alert
get.description:
Returns an operator-only, tenant-scoped watcher projection in canonical
bytewise displayName then userId order.
Customer contacts are never watchers
and never appear in this projection. The backend reloads the Alert and
re-evaluates the caller's live scoped alert.read authority on every read.

200.description: Current canonical Alert watcher page.

put.summary: Add one eligible operator as an Alert watcher
put.description:
The target user must be an active member of this tenant, represent a human
operator rather than a customer contact, and retain live scoped alert.read
authority for this exact Alert when the command commits. The backend
re-resolves both caller and target under the authorization-state lock.
If-Match binds the current Alert version. An exact idempotent replay returns
its immutable watcher-page result. Adding an existing watcher is a successful
set-idempotent no-op that returns the unchanged page and version.

200.description: Watcher added once, or the exact immutable result replayed.

delete.summary: Remove one Alert watcher
delete.description:
Removal is permitted for an existing watcher even if the target user is now
inactive or no longer eligible to read the Alert; the target is not resolved
through an active-user picker. Caller authority and Alert version remain live
checks. An exact idempotent replay returns its immutable watcher-page result;
removing a non-watcher is a successful set-idempotent no-op that returns the
unchanged page and version.

200.description: Watcher removed once, or the exact immutable result replayed.

post.summary: Apply one allowlisted transition from the Alert workflow version
post.description:
The backend reloads the Alert, its pinned Alert workflow version, roles,
permissions, required comment, and required custom fields. UI-displayed
actions are hints only. If-Match and expectedVersion must identify the same
current version. An exact authorized idempotency replay returns the current
projection without duplicating activity, audit, SLA, or notification effects.

200.description: Transition applied once and all planned side effects committed atomically.

post.summary: Close an Alert through one terminal workflow transition
post.description:
Uses the same pinned workflow, authorization, optimistic concurrency, and
idempotency rules as the generic transition command, while additionally
requiring the current state to be non-terminal and the requested target
state to be terminal. The transition key and all workflow requirements are
still validated by the backend before the atomic commit.

200.description: Terminal transition applied once and all planned side effects committed atomically.

post.summary: Reopen an Alert through one validated workflow transition
post.description:
Uses the same pinned workflow, authorization, optimistic concurrency, and
idempotency rules as the generic transition command, while additionally
requiring a terminal current state and a non-terminal target reached by a
workflow transition declared as reopen. Clients cannot supply or override
that server-side workflow intent.

200.description: Reopen transition applied once and all planned side effects committed atomically.

post.summary: Assign an Alert to an authorized operator team and optional user

200.description: Assignment and its closed side-effect plan committed atomically.

post.summary: Atomically claim an Alert for the current operator
post.description:
Claim authority, team membership, workflow state, expectedVersion, and the
unclaimed predicate are evaluated in the same atomic write. Exactly one
contender receives 200 with the persisted winner; every loser receives 409.
A stale UI claim action never authorizes or predicts the winner.

200.description: The current operator is the single persisted claim winner.

post.summary: Release the current Alert claim

200.description: Claim released and all planned side effects committed atomically.

post.summary: Transfer an Alert to another authorized team or assignee

200.description: Transfer and all planned side effects committed atomically.

post.summary: Idempotently link one or more Alerts to a new or existing Case
post.description:
Alert and Case remain independent aggregates. The path Alert must appear
exactly once in sources; If-Match and expectedVersion bind that source,
while every additional source carries its own expected version. The backend
rechecks current alert.escalate authority, target-case authority, source
visibility, and every copy selection on both first execution and replay.
Exact authorized replays return the same Case/link identities without
duplicating copied data, activity, audit, SLA, or notification effects.
The response ETag always identifies the current path Alert; the Case and
every source snapshot carry their own explicit versions in the body.

200.description: Alerts linked once to the authorized existing Case, or an exact replay of that result.

201.description: New Case created and all Alert links and selected copies committed once, or an exact replay of that result.

post.summary: Idempotently link an Alert to an existing Case
post.description:
This explicit action accepts only an existing_case target and never
creates a Case. It uses the same pinned escalation planner and atomic
persistence boundary as escalation, reauthorizes alert.escalate and
case.update from one live authority snapshot, and binds every source,
version, copy selection, and target to the idempotency fingerprint.
Exact authorized replays return the original receipt without inserting
another link or copied item. A pair retracted by unlink is terminal and
any later attempt to link that Alert and Case returns 409 Conflict.

200.description: Alert linked once to the existing Case, or the exact historical receipt replayed.

post.summary: Idempotently retract an Alert and Case link
post.description:
Appends an immutable tenant-scoped retraction and never updates or
deletes the historical Alert/Case link. If-Match must equal the body
expectedVersion for the Alert, while expectedCaseVersion independently
protects the Case. The commit reauthorizes alert.escalate and
case.update, applies compare-and-swap to both aggregates, increments
both versions, and emits activity, audit, and outbox evidence for each.
Exact payload-bound replays return the original receipt without new
side effects. The same Alert/Case pair cannot be linked again.

200.description: Immutable retraction and both aggregate version transitions committed once.

get.summary: List explicit Alert duplicate and correlation evidence
get.description:
Returns active and retracted Alert-to-Alert relations only after both
Alerts satisfy alert.read and alert.update at one common live scope.
Authorization filtering happens before the UUIDv7 cursor and page limit.
A relation never merges, closes, or rewrites either Alert.

200.description: Bounded newest-first immutable relation evidence.

post.summary: Explicitly classify two Alerts as duplicate or correlated
post.description:
Creates immutable, reason-bearing relation evidence and never silently
merges either Alert. If-Match binds the path Alert while the body pins
the related Alert. The commit reauthorizes alert.read and alert.update
at one common scope, applies CAS to both versions, increments both, and
atomically appends activity, audit, and outbox evidence for each Alert.
Exact payload-bound replays return the original receipt without writes.

200.description: Relation and both version transitions committed once, or exactly replayed.

post.summary: Append a terminal retraction for an Alert relation
post.description:
Retraction never updates or deletes the original relation. If-Match
binds the path Alert and the body pins the related Alert. The atomic
commit increments both versions and appends activity, audit, outbox,
and one immutable retraction. A retracted pair cannot be linked again.

200.description: Immutable retraction and both version transitions committed once, or exactly replayed.

get.summary: List server-projected Alert comments
get.description: Lists the operator-only Alert conversation after live comment-read authorization. Customer-safe public comments use the dedicated portal route and cannot inhabit this path.

200.description: A bounded operator-only comment page.

post.summary: Idempotently add a public or operator-private Alert comment
post.description:
This operator-only route accepts public or private visibility. Public creation
requires alert.comment.public; private creation additionally requires
alert.comment.private. Markdown is sanitized server-side and arbitrary HTML
is rejected. Private content is excluded from customer UI, API, email,
webhook, and export projections before pagination or template rendering.
Customer principals use the dedicated customer-portal operation.

201.description: Comment created once. An exact replay preserves comment identity, revision, and immutable content while canEdit is recomputed fail-closed from current authority.

post.summary: Preview one bounded Alert comment without side effects
post.description: Resolves attachment and mention projections against the same live Alert authority used by create, sanitizes Markdown, and performs no write, audit, activity, notification, or idempotency reservation.

200.description: Server-accepted Markdown plus sanitized HTML and resolved safe projections; no state was changed.

get.summary: List non-oracular mention candidates for one Alert
get.description: Returns only active human operators already eligible to be mentioned on this exact Alert after live Alert read and tenant authority checks. Empty results do not reveal whether hidden identities or tickets exist; the list is ticket-scoped authorization output, never a tenant directory.

200.description: Bounded ticket-scoped active-human candidate page in canonical bytewise order.

patch.summary: Append one author-only Alert comment revision
patch.description: Appends a new immutable child revision only for a directly authored origin=api comment when the authenticated human operator is the frozen original author, the 15-minute window remains open, the exact comment revision ETag matches, visibility is unchanged, and every mention and attachment is re-authorized against the same live Alert. escalation_copy and system comments are immutable. There is no delete, visibility change, or administrator override.

200.description: Newly appended immutable revision, or the pinned identity, revision, and immutable content for an exact replay. canEdit is recomputed fail-closed and is never replayed as a stale capability.

get.summary: List immutable Alert comment revision history
get.description: Returns a caller-safe projection of append-only revisions. Operator projections may contain authorized private attachment and mention snapshots; customer fields are structurally absent.

200.description: Newest-first immutable revision page.

200.description: Newest-first bounded Alert activity page after live resource authorization.

200.description: Bounded activity page in the caller's safe projection.

post.summary: Reserve a short-lived server-generated TOTP enrollment
post.description:
Requires the external deployment bootstrap token. The TOTP secret is
generated by the server, encrypted before persistence, and returned once.
No user or password credential is created by this operation.

post.description:
Consumes the deployment and enrollment tokens. User, password credential,
confirmed TOTP credential, recovery codes, protected platform role, initial
session, and platform audit event are committed together exactly once.

post.description: Unknown identities and invalid passwords produce the same response.

post.summary: Authenticate an existing platform identity through global LDAP and mandatory local TOTP
post.description:
Authenticates the directory password against one enabled platform-global
LDAP provider, resolves exactly one pre-existing active Periapsis user,
requires that user's already-enrolled local TOTP factor, applies only
allowlisted non-superadmin mapping rules, and commits the identity link,
source-owned grants, provenance, session, and redacted audit atomically.
It never creates a User and never issues a weaker MFA continuation.
Missing or ambiguous identity, missing TOTP enrollment, empty mapping,
invalid credentials, and identity collisions share a non-enumerating denial.

303.description: Platform LDAP and local TOTP accepted; continue to the canonical same-origin return path.

post.summary: Authenticate through one tenant LDAP directory
post.description:
The browser posts the directory password only to this synchronous,
tenant-bound endpoint. The server rejects every pre-existing bearer,
session, MFA, federation-transaction, and continuation authority;
applies anonymous network, account, and provider throttles; authenticates
against the pinned LDAP snapshot; and atomically reconciles the JIT
identity before issuing either a session or an MFA continuation. The
password is owned by this request, is never logged or persisted, and is
destroyed before the handler returns. Authentication, locator, account,
and mapping denials share one non-enumerating response.

303.description: Continue to the canonical local return path or fixed local MFA continuation marker.

post.summary: Start one anonymous tenant OIDC Authorization Code ceremony
post.description:
The server resolves the tenant and provider only from the canonical public
locator, meters the attempt, replaces any prior browser-bound OIDC
transaction, and redirects only to the immutable HTTPS authorization
endpoint pinned by the protocol kernel. Authorization headers, existing
session authority, and existing MFA-continuation authority are rejected.
The browser must send an exact same-origin Origin or Referer; this endpoint
is not a CORS surface.

303.description: Continue the one-time OIDC ceremony at the pinned IdP endpoint.

get.summary: Complete one browser-bound OIDC callback
get.description:
The raw query string is delivered unchanged to the strict OIDC kernel so
duplicate, conflicting, malformed, or oversized artifacts fail closed. The
exact host-only transaction cookie is required and cleared on every attempt.
Authorization headers, existing session authority, and existing
MFA-continuation authority are rejected.
A successful session is revalidated through the ordinary authentication
boundary before the normal SameSite=Strict session cookie is emitted.

303.description: Continue to the stored canonical local return path, or to the fixed local MFA continuation marker.

post.summary: Start one anonymous direct-platform OIDC Authorization Code ceremony
post.description:
The server resolves one enabled direct-platform OIDC provider only from the
canonical public provider key, which conveys no authority. It meters the
attempt, replaces any prior direct-platform browser-bound OIDC transaction,
and redirects only to the immutable HTTPS authorization endpoint pinned by
the protocol kernel. Authorization and bearer headers, existing session
authority, and existing federated MFA-continuation authority are rejected.
The browser must send an exact same-origin Origin or Referer; this endpoint
is not a CORS surface. Only an exact live pre-linked provider account may
finish the ceremony; provider claims never link an account, select a tenant,
or grant platform authority.

303.description: Continue the one-time direct-platform OIDC ceremony at the pinned IdP endpoint.

get.summary: Complete one browser-bound direct-platform OIDC callback
get.description:
The exact raw query string is delivered unchanged to the strict OIDC kernel
so duplicate, conflicting, malformed, or oversized artifacts fail closed at
the documented byte ceiling. The exact direct-platform host-only transaction
cookie is required and cleared on every attempt. Authorization and bearer
headers, existing session authority, and existing federated MFA-continuation
authority are rejected; this cross-site top-level callback is the sole
exception to the start operation's same-origin boundary.
A successful exact pre-linked account either establishes a direct `oidc`
session with no active tenant or emits the common federated MFA continuation.
Later tenant selection requires live admission through an exact binding to
this provider and rotates both session credential and primary provenance.

303.description: Continue to the stored canonical local return path, or to the fixed local MFA continuation marker.

post.summary: Start one anonymous direct-platform SAML SP-initiated ceremony
post.description:
The server resolves one enabled direct-platform SAML provider only from
the canonical public provider key, which conveys no authority. It meters
the attempt, replaces any prior browser-bound direct-platform SAML
transaction, and redirects only to the immutable HTTPS SSO endpoint pinned
by the protocol kernel. Authorization and bearer headers, existing session
authority, and existing federated MFA-continuation authority are rejected.
The browser must send an exact same-origin Origin or Referer; this endpoint
is not a CORS surface and IdP-initiated login is unsupported. Only an exact
live pre-linked provider account may finish the ceremony; provider claims
never link an account, select a tenant, or grant platform authority.

303.description: Continue the one-time direct-platform SAML ceremony at the pinned IdP endpoint.

post.summary: Complete one browser-bound direct-platform SAML HTTP POST ACS
post.description:
The exact bounded application/x-www-form-urlencoded body is delivered

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one opaque non-secret retry key is required; duplicate or comma-folded
field values are rejected. The key is scoped to the authenticated actor and
authorization context (platform or tenant), and to the operation. Replay
behavior is guaranteed only for the retention window documented by that
operation; this reusable parameter does not promise indefinite replay. During
that window, an exact non-secret replay can return the same resource's current
representation and current strong ETag without undoing later mutations, while
an exact one-time credential issue or rotation replay instead returns 409 and
redacted metadata without the bearer token. Reuse with a different request
representation returns 409 during the documented window. After expiry, the
request can be evaluated as a new command subject to the operation's documented
uniqueness and conflict safeguards.

AuditOperationReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
AuditOperationReason.description:
Mandatory already-redacted reason for an audit export, retention, or legal-hold
mutation. Exactly one visible-ASCII value is accepted, excluding comma and
leading or trailing spaces. Secrets, tokens, credentials, assertions, personal
identifiers, and customer payloads are forbidden. The reason is written to the
corresponding audit stream in the same transaction and is never reflected.

PlatformOperationsAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
PlatformOperationsAuditReason.description:
Mandatory non-secret reason for a global-settings or feature-flag mutation.
Exactly one visible-ASCII value excluding comma and leading or trailing
spaces is accepted. The reason is appended only to redacted platform audit
in the mutation transaction and is never reflected.

TenantSettingsAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
TenantSettingsAuditReason.description:
Mandatory non-secret reason for changing tenant identity or regional settings.
Exactly one visible-ASCII value is accepted, excluding comma and leading or
trailing spaces. Secrets, tokens, credentials, assertions, personal identifiers,
and customer payloads are forbidden. The value is recorded only in tenant audit.

TicketNumberingAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
TicketNumberingAuditReason.description:
Mandatory non-secret reason for publishing an Alert or Case numbering
policy. Exactly one visible-ASCII value is accepted, excluding comma and
leading or trailing spaces. Secrets, tokens, credentials, assertions,
personal identifiers, and customer payloads are forbidden. The value is
recorded only in the tenant audit stream and is never reflected.

WebhookUrlPolicyIfMatch.name: If-Match
WebhookUrlPolicyIfMatch.description:

exactly "v0"; an existing policy requires its current positive version.
Weak, wildcard, folded, overflowing, or non-canonical values are rejected.

WebhookUrlPolicyAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
WebhookUrlPolicyAuditReason.description:
Mandatory non-secret reason for changing the webhook egress boundary.
Exactly one visible-ASCII value is accepted, excluding comma and leading
or trailing spaces. Hostnames, URLs, tokens, credentials, personal
identifiers, and customer payloads are forbidden. The value is written
only to the redacted tenant audit stream and is never reflected.

PlatformLocalAccountIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
PlatformLocalAccountIdempotencyKey.description:

account with replayed=true and never re-emits a one-time invitation/recovery
token or re-runs password/factor verification. Reuse with changed public or
keyed-secret request material returns 409.

PlatformLocalAccountAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
PlatformLocalAccountAuditReason.description:

value is accepted, excluding comma and leading/trailing spaces. Passwords,
tokens, factor proofs, recovery codes, identifiers, and customer data are
forbidden. The reason is written only to redacted platform audit.

PlatformIdentityProviderAuditReason.name: X-Audit-Reason
PlatformIdentityProviderAuditReason.description:
Mandatory non-secret, already-redacted operator reason for a platform identity-
provider, provider-account, or explicit tenant-binding mutation. Exactly one field value is accepted; duplicate or comma-
folded values are rejected. The transport value is visible ASCII only (space
through tilde), excluding comma, with no leading or trailing space. Never include secrets, tokens, credentials,
assertions, claims, subjects, metadata, or customer data. The reason is appended
to platform audit in the same mutation transaction and is never reflected.

LDAPProviderIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
LDAPProviderIdempotencyKey.description:
Exactly one opaque non-secret retry key is required; duplicate or comma-folded
field values are rejected. The key is scoped to the authenticated actor, tenant,
and LDAP-provider create operation. An exact payload-bound replay returns the
same resource Location without asserting its current representation or version;
reuse with a different request representation returns 409.

DfirResourceIfMatch.name: If-Match
DfirResourceIfMatch.description: Exact current strong DFIR subresource ETag within the bigint-backed JSON safe-integer range. The terminal revision is not incrementable and is rejected for mutations. Weak, wildcard, folded, overflowing, or mismatched values are rejected.

MetadataIfMatch.name: If-Match

remain incrementable as a positive PostgreSQL int4, so v2147483647 is not
a valid metadata-mutation precondition. Weak, wildcard, folded, overflowing,
or mismatched values are rejected; omission returns 428 and mismatch returns 412.

TicketWatcherIfMatch.name: If-Match
TicketWatcherIfMatch.description:
Exact current strong Alert or Case version ETag for a watcher mutation.
The current version must remain incrementable as a positive PostgreSQL
int4, so v2147483647 is not accepted. Weak, wildcard, duplicate, folded,
overflowing, or mismatched values are rejected; omission returns 428 and
mismatch returns 412.

PlatformAuthProviderAccountIfMatch.name: If-Match
PlatformAuthProviderAccountIfMatch.description:
The current composite provider-account ETag. It must encode the same
account expectedVersion carried by the request body and the exact
embedded user-profile version returned by the read. Weak, wildcard,
folded, account-version-only, noncanonical, and overflowing validators
are rejected; omission returns 428 and a stale account or user version
returns 412.

PlatformLocalAccountIfMatch.name: If-Match
PlatformLocalAccountIfMatch.description:
Exact strong local-account validator. It must encode the same expectedRevision
carried by the body. Missing values return 428; a stale locked revision returns
412; weak, wildcard, duplicate, folded, or noncanonical values are rejected.

PlatformAuthProviderTenantBindingIfMatch.name: If-Match
PlatformAuthProviderTenantBindingIfMatch.description:
The current composite tenant-binding ETag. It must encode the same binding
expectedVersion and live tenant-summary expectedTenantVersion carried by
the request body. Weak, wildcard, folded, version-only, noncanonical, and
overflowing validators are rejected; omission returns 428 and a stale
binding or tenant version returns 412.

SavedViewIfMatch.name: If-Match
SavedViewIfMatch.description:
The current representation-bound saved-view ETag. It must match the exact
resource and specification digest while the request body carries the same
positive expectedRevision. Weak, wildcard, folded, and version-only
validators are rejected; omission returns 428 and mismatch returns 412.

WorkflowIfMatch.name: If-Match
WorkflowIfMatch.description:
The current workflow catalog ETag. It must encode the same lineage and
expectedRevision as the request body; weak, wildcard, folded, and version-only
validators are rejected. Omission returns 428 and mismatch returns 412.

IfMatchOptional.name: If-Match
IfMatchOptional.description:
Omitted only when creating the singleton for the first time. If a current
configuration exists, omission returns 428, mismatch returns 412, and wildcards
or weak validators are rejected.

EdgeIfMatch.name: If-Match
EdgeIfMatch.description:
The current representation-bound authorization-edge ETag obtained from the
resource body or response header. Wildcards, weak validators, and version-only
validators are not accepted. Omission returns 428 and mismatch returns 412.
